summary: Repeated supplied-harness relaunches reached chat, preserved the visible Claude Plan model/provider and connected account, and returned RESTART_OK. The full case is blocked because native app-shortcut relaunch could not be exercised through this interface.

observed_checks.check: Relaunch reaches chat without automatic /providers screen (harness subset)
observed_checks.observation: The second and third supplied-harness launches displayed the chat composer directly; no /providers screen appeared.

observed_checks.check: Selected provider/model visibly match before and after relaunch
observed_checks.observation: Visible /status output showed Claude Fable 5.1 Plan with Claude Plan before and after relaunch.
Visible /status output showed Claude Plan account connected before and after relaunch.

observed_checks.check: Exact request returns RESTART_OK after relaunch
observed_checks.observation: The visible assistant response was RESTART_OK.
The native Applications shortcut is inaccessible through this interface; only the supplied TMUX harness launch was exercised.

blockers: Native Applications shortcut and macOS Desktop placement are inaccessible through this interface, so the required native-shortcut relaunch cannot be verified.
actions: Started and relaunched only the supplied target session with the provided TMUX command.
Used raw TMUX literal text plus separate Enter key actions for /status and the exact request.
Exited the target session with Ctrl-C after each exercised run; no target server remained.
Recorded the complete key/action history in actions.log.
limitations: The first harness launch showed a visible one-time directory trust prompt; it was accepted per the prompt before baseline observation.
Only visible /status provider/account metadata was evaluated; no hidden credential state or native keychain prompt was inspected.
The supplied harness launch is not substituted for the required native app-shortcut launch.
test_instruction_ambiguity: The instruction to quit normally did not identify a visible quit command or key; the visible slash-command list had no quit entry, and Ctrl-C exited the target session.
